subject: Agriculture
title: Perennial Grains
description: A short lesson to help you apply Perennial Grains.

hook.text: What if wheat didn't need replanting every year? Perennial grains could end annual tillage forever.

buildup.text: Annual crops require plowing, seeding, and establishment every season—exposing soil to erosion each time.

discovery.text: Kernza, a perennial wheat relative, regrows from its roots for 3–5 years. No replanting, no tillage.

twist.text: Perennial roots grow 3 meters deep—holding soil, storing carbon, and accessing water annuals can't reach.

climax.text: Kernza yields are still only 25% of annual wheat. Decades of breeding lie ahead before it competes.

punchline.text: A grain you plant once and harvest for years. It exists—it just needs work.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of perennial grains like Kernza?
options: They regrow from roots without annual replanting, preventing erosion
